Definition: apparently a primary word; a stone (literally or figuratively):--(mill-, stumbling-)stone.
BiblicalUsage: líthos means a stone, and Scripture puts it to work in every part of life. In Matthew 21:42, "The stone which the builders rejected"; and in 1 Peter 2:4, "[as unto] a living stone". In 1 Peter 2:6, "I lay in Sion a chief corner stone"; and in 1 Corinthians 3:12, "precious stones".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ is the stone the builders refused and God made the head of the corner — the living stone, chosen and precious. I hold that we are lively stones built into a spiritual house, and that the same stone is a stumbling stone to the disobedient. My position is that I will build on Him and Him only, because every other foundation is wood, hay, and stubble.
